Retrospective comparative cohort study.

Methods

90 eyes of 45 patients who underwent bilateral cataract surgery after myopic LASIK were classified according to implanted IOL type: Full-DOFi Smooth (Tecnis Synergy), Partial-DOFi Enhanced (Eyhance), and Partial-DOFi Extended IOLs (PureSee). Distance-corrected visual acuity, monocular distance-corrected defocus curves, DOFi at 0.2 logMAR, refractive predictability with Barrett True-K TK and Haigis TK after IOL-specific optimization or mean prediction error zeroing, and patient-reported satisfaction were evaluated 3 months postoperatively.

Results

Corrected distance and intermediate visual acuities were comparable among groups (P = .967 and .780), whereas corrected near visual acuity differed (P < .001), favoring Full-DOFi Smooth, followed by Partial-DOFi Extended and Partial-DOFi Enhanced. DOFi was 3.22, 2.23, and 1.56 D, respectively. Prediction errors within ±0.50 D ranged from 76.7% to 83.3% with Barrett True-K TK and 70.0% to 73.3% with Haigis TK. Eyetemis analysis showed no trueness differences; Barrett True-K TK showed better precision and accuracy only in the Full-DOFi Smooth group. Near-vision satisfaction differed among groups, whereas pairwise glare/halo differences were not significant.

Conclusion

In selected post-myopic LASIK eyes, expected DOFi-based functional differences remained evident after correction of residual refractive error. Barrett True-K TK and Haigis TK showed generally comparable refractive performance. These findings indicate that DOFi-based functional classification remains clinically relevant in eyes with previous myopic LASIK.

records.title: Alignment Between Corneal Biomechanical Anisotropy and Toricity Using Optical Coherence Elastography.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Alignment Between Corneal Biomechanical Anisotropy and Toricity Using Optical Coherence Elastography.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the agreement in orientation and magnitude between corneal toricity and biomechanical anisotropy using optical coherence elastography (OCE).

Setting

College of Optometry, University of Houston, Houston, Texas, USA.

Design

Prospective cross-sectional study.

Methods

Healthy participants with spherical refractive error or corneal astigmatism > 0.50D were included. Corneal radial mechanical wave propagation speed, a proxy for corneal shear modulus, was measured using air-pulse wave-based OCE imaging (30° intervals over 360°). Biomechanical principal meridian () was defined as meridian with greatest wave speed, and its magnitude was calculated as difference between principal and orthogonal meridians. Likewise, astigmatic principal meridian () was defined as steep corneal meridian from videokeratography, and its magnitude was defined as dioptric difference between orthogonal steep and flat meridians. To compare these different domains (biomechanical anisotropy and astigmatism) within and across subjects, both vector magnitudes were cohort-normalized. Directional alignment between and was assessed using polar double-angle plots. Vectorial difference between these measures quantified similarities in both orientation and magnitude.

Results

30 eyes from 30 subjects were studied. Corneal astigmatism ranged from 0.15 to 3.66D (1.4±0.8D; mean±SD). Corneal wave speed in steep meridian was faster (12.97±1.6m/s) compared to flat meridian(9.03±1.8m/s). Biomechanical anisotropy strongly correlated with astigmatism (R2 = 0.88). Angular difference between and was 6.0°±7.1° among astigmatic eyes. Cohort-normalized magnitude difference between and was 0.06±0.07.

Conclusions

In vivo human corneal wave-based OCE measurements demonstrate that corneal biomechanical anisotropy exhibits an orthogonal pattern, highly correlated in orientation and magnitude with corneal topography.

records.title: Intraocular lens power calculation formula accuracy in 1178 eyes with short axial length: systematic review and network meta-analysis.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Intraocular lens power calculation formula accuracy in 1178 eyes with short axial length: systematic review and network meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Topic

To systematically review the literature and conduct a comprehensive quantitative analysis to compare the accuracy of different intraocular lens (IOL) calculation formulas in eyes with short axial lengths (ALs).

Clinical relevance

The precision of the IOL formulas decreases when applied in eyes with short AL (AL <22 mm), and many new formulas for calculating IOL power have been proposed in the past few decades. However, the accuracy of these formulas has not been systematically compared when applied in eyes with short AL.

Methods

This study systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library databases to collect relevant research literature published between January 2003 and September 2023. Included were prospective or retrospective clinical studies involving cataract patients with short AL (AL <22 mm) and reporting the following outcomes: mean absolute error, median absolute error (MedAE), and percentage of eyes with a prediction error (PE) within ±0.25 diopters (D), ±0.50 D, and ±1.00 D. A network meta-analysis was performed using R software (v. 4.2.1).

Results

15 prospective or retrospective studies involving 1178 eyes and 12 calculation formulas were included in this study. The network meta-analysis showed that compared with the widely used Haigis formula, the Kane formula had a higher percentage of eyes with PE within the range of ±0.25 D, ±0.50 D, and ±1.00 D (all odds ratio >1, but P > .05). In addition, based on the surface under the cumulative ranking area (SUCRA), the Kane formula had the highest probability of predicting the PE of the eyes within the range of ±0.25 D, with its SUCRA value of 95.74%, followed by Haigis formula (94.79%) and Olsen Standalone formula (84.04%). The Kane and Olsen Standalone formulas had the lowest MedAE.

Conclusions

The Kane, Haigis, and Olsen Standalone formulas may perform better than other formulas in calculating the IOLs power in eyes with short AL. Nonetheless, significant uncertainty remains in this area. The accuracy of these formulas in patients with short AL needs to be verified by large multicenter registry studies.

records.title: Use of intracameral antibiotics prophylaxis in patients with posterior capsular rupture during cataract surgery: systematic review and meta-analysis.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Use of intracameral antibiotics prophylaxis in patients with posterior capsular rupture during cataract surgery: systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Topic

Posterior capsular rupture (PCR) during cataract surgery predisposes patients to postoperative endophthalmitis (POE). However, little is known about the prophylactic use of intracameral antibiotics (ICA) to prevent POE after PCR. This systematic review and meta-analysis assesed the efficacy of ICA in preventing POE in patients with PCR.

Clinical relevance

PCR increases the risk of POE by more than 6-fold, emphasizing the need for targeted prophylactic strategies. This study focused on the clinical importance of ICA in reducing the incidence of POE in this high-risk population.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane were searched for articles published up to May 21, 2024, with the following strategy: (cataract OR phaco OR "Cataract Extraction" OR "manual small incision cataract surgery" OR phacoemulsification OR "extracapsular cataract extraction" OR ECCE) AND (intracameral OR "Intracameral Injection" OR "irrigating infusion fluid" OR "anterior chamber injection") AND (antibiotic OR moxifloxacin OR cefuroxime OR vancomycin OR cephalosporin OR prophylaxis). Studies were included that reported the incidence of endophthalmitis in patients with PCR during cataract surgery and a comparison of prophylactic ICA with no ICA. Statistical analysis was conducted using R software v. 4.3.2. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024558144).

Results

The initial search yielded 1660 results. After removing duplicate records and ineligible studies, 193 remained and were thoroughly reviewed based on the inclusion criteria. 9 studies consisting of 2 randomized controlled trials and 7 observational studies were included in the meta-analysis. There were a total of 153 690 patients, with 50 207 (33.6%) patients in the ICA group and 103 483 (67.3%) in the no ICA group. There was a significantly lower incidence of endophthalmitis in the ICA group (odds ratio [OR] 0.41; 95% CI 0.26-0.65; P < .001; I2 = 9%). Independently, the use of prophylactic intracameral moxifloxacin was also related to a lower risk of endophthalmitis (OR 0.33; 95% CI 0.19-0.57; P < .001; I2 = 33%).

Conclusions

The findings suggest that the use of ICA is efficient in preventing postoperative endophthalmitis in patients who had PCR during cataract surgery.

records.title: SURGICAL OUTCOMES OF LAMELLAR MACULAR HOLE EYES WITH OR WITHOUT PRESERVATION OF LAMELLAR HOLE-ASSOCIATED EPIRETINAL PROLIFERATION TECHNIQUE: A Meta-analysis.

content.title: SURGICAL OUTCOMES OF LAMELLAR MACULAR HOLE EYES WITH OR WITHOUT PRESERVATION OF LAMELLAR HOLE-ASSOCIATED EPIRETINAL PROLIFERATION TECHNIQUE: A Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate sparing or embedding technique for lamellar hole-associated epiretinal proliferation and in comparison with traditional internal limiting membrane and epiretinal membrane peeling in lamellar macular holes.

Methods

PubMed, Web of Science, Medline, EMBASE, Cochrane, CNKI, Wan Fang, and VIP Databases (PROSPERO number CRD42024466392) were searched. Trials of various lamellar hole-associated epiretinal proliferation removal or preservation techniques in lamellar macular holes were included (case reports of only 1 case excluded). Postoperative changes in best-corrected visual acuity were calculated. Central retinal thickness and number of patients with new postoperative intact ellipsoid zones were secondary outcomes.

Results

Eight studies were eligible and four compared with peeling groups. Preservation groups showed a significant visual improvement operatively (mean difference = -0.25 logMAR; 95% confidence interval = -0.30 to -0.21; P < 0.00001) and improved compared with peeling groups (mean difference = -0.19 logMAR; 95% confidence interval = -0.29 to -0.1; P < 0.0001). In addition, the number of patients with intact ellipsoid zones increased in the preserving groups (odd ratio = 2.55; 95% confidence interval = 1.48-4.38; P = 0.0007) and also increased compared with peeling groups (odd ratio =10.80; 95% confidence interval = 1.86-62.83; P = 0.008).

Conclusion

Based on the current evidence, lamellar hole-associated epiretinal proliferation sparing or embedding technique has favorable postoperative outcomes compared with peeling technique for lamellar macular holes.

records.title: Fibrin Glue Versus Sutures for Securing Conjunctival Autograft in Primary Pterygium Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Fibrin Glue Versus Sutures for Securing Conjunctival Autograft in Primary Pterygium Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Topic

This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates whether fibrin glue provides superior outcomes compared to sutures for securing conjunctival autografts in primary pterygium surgery. We focused on recurrence rates, operative time, postoperative complications, and patient discomfort.

Clinical relevance

Pterygium recurrence and postoperative morbidity remain significant concerns in ocular surface surgery. A growing number of surgeons are adopting fibrin glue instead of sutures to anchor conjunctival autografts, but the evidence on comparative effectiveness has evolved in recent years. This updated analysis aims to guide surgical practice with the most current data.

Methods

We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, and CINAHL on 8 November 2024. We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing fibrin glue versus sutures in primary pterygium surgery. Studies were screened, selected, and data-extracted by two independent reviewers. Meta-analysis was performed using a random-effects model. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool. The review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines and registered on PROSPERO (ID: CRD42024520625).

Results

Twenty RCTs were included. Fibrin glue significantly reduced recurrence risk compared to sutures (pooled odds ratio: 2.46; 95% CI: 1.06-5.69; 27 P  =  .0352; I2 = 0%). Operative time was significantly shorter with fibrin glue (pooled mean difference: 15.65 29 minutes; 95% CI: 11.45-19.86; P < .005; I2 = 99.29%). Pain scores at postoperative day 1 were significantly lower with fibrin glue compared with sutures (pooled standardized mean difference: 1.32; 95% CI: -2.11 to -0.52; p < .001; I2 = 90%). Rates of graft retraction were inconsistent between the two groups, while subconjunctival hemorrhages were more common in the suture group.

Conclusion

Fibrin glue is associated with lower recurrence rates, reduced operative time, and less postoperative discomfort than sutures in primary pterygium surgery. However, variability in graft retraction outcomes warrants further investigation. These findings support the broader adoption of fibrin glue as a preferred technique for conjunctival autograft fixation in routine clinical practice.

records.title: Network Meta-analysis of Intraocular Lens Power Calculation Formula Accuracy in 1016 Eyes With Long Axial Length.

content.title: Network Meta-analysis of Intraocular Lens Power Calculation Formula Accuracy in 1016 Eyes With Long Axial Length.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To systematically review the literature and quantitatively synthesize the currently available evidence to compare the accuracy of different intraocular lens calculation formulas in eyes with long axial length (AL).

Design

Network meta-analysis.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched for studies published between January 2000 and June 2022. Included were prospective or retrospective clinical studies reporting the following outcomes in cataract patients with long AL (ie, ≥26 mm): percentage of eyes with a prediction error (PE) within ±0.25, ±0.50, and ±1.00 diopters (D). Network meta-analysis was conducted using R software (version 4.2.1).

Results

Ten prospective or retrospective clinical studies, including 1016 eyes and 11 calculation formulas, were identified. A traditional meta-analysis showed that for the percentage of eyes with PE within ±0.25 and ±0.50 D, the Olsen, Kane, and Emmetropia Verifying Optical (EVO) all had insignificantly higher percentages compared with others. Considering the percentage of eyes with PE within ±1.00 D, the original and modified Wang-Koch adjustment formulas for Holladay 1 (H1-WK and H1-MWK) and EVO formulas showed superiority, but the difference was insignificant. This network meta-analysis revealed that compared with the widely used Barrett Universal II (BUII) formula, the Olsen, Kane, and EVO formulas had higher percentages of eyes with PE within ±0.25, ±0.50, and ±1.00 D (all odds ratios >1 but P >.05). Based on the surface under the cumulative ranking area (SUCRA) values for the percentage of eyes with PE within ±0.25 D, the Olsen (96.4%), Kane (77.5%), and EVO (75.9%) formulas had the highest probability of being in the top 3 of the 11 formulas.

Conclusions

The Olsen, Kane, and EVO formulas may perform better than others in calculating IOL power in eyes with long AL. Nevertheless, there is still considerable uncertainty in this regard and the accuracy of these formulas in highly myopic eyes should be confirmed in studies based on large multicenter registries.

records.title: High-Dose Intravitreal Topotecan for Refractory or Recurrent Retinoblastoma: Efficacy, Safety and Intraocular Cytokine Profiles.

content.title: High-Dose Intravitreal Topotecan for Refractory or Recurrent Retinoblastoma: Efficacy, Safety and Intraocular Cytokine Profiles.
content.abstract:
Objective

To evaluate the outcomes and safety of high-dose intravitreal topotecan (100 μg, IVitT100) in the treatment of refractory or recurrent intraocular retinoblastoma (RB).

Design

Prospective, non-comparative case series.

Participants

15 consecutive patients (15 eyes) with refractory or recurrent RB at the Eye & ENT Hospital of Fudan University between October 2023 and September 2025.

Methods

Participants received IVitT100 every four weeks. Clinical characteristics were recorded before and after treatment. Tumor control and injection-related complications were assessed at each visit. Aqueous humor cytokines and electroretinography (ERG) were analyzed to evaluate inflammatory changes and retinal function.

Main outcome measures

Treatment outcomes, including intraretinal tumor and intraocular seeds control, globe salvage rate, and ocular and systemic adverse events, were assessed during follow-up.

Results

At a median follow-up of 9 months (IQR, 6.0-14.0) after the final intravitreal injection, high-dose intravitreal topotecan achieved a globe salvage rate of 93%, with complete control of intraocular seeds in all eyes (100%) and complete regression of intraretinal tumors in 3 of 4 eyes (75%). Baseline ERG amplitude was 5.7 μV (IQR, 1.5-14.7), post-treatment amplitude was 5.7 μV (IQR, 1.9-15.8), showing no significant retinal function impairment (P = 0.429). None of the 27 cytokines showed significant changes between pre- and post-treatment measurements in RB eyes (all P > 0.05). No severe ocular or systemic adverse events were reported.

Conclusions

IVitT100 is highly effective for refractory or recurrent RB with vitreous seeds, subretinal seeds, and intraretinal tumors. It exhibits minimal retinal toxicity and does not induce intraocular inflammatory responses, supporting its role as a safe and effective first-line intravitreal therapy for advanced RB.

records.title: Conflicts of Interest Transparency, Study Outcomes, and Risk of Bias in Myopia Controlled Trials: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Conflicts of Interest Transparency, Study Outcomes, and Risk of Bias in Myopia Controlled Trials: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Topic

To determine whether the transparency of conflicts of interest (COI) declarations is associated with study outcomes and methodological quality in randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of myopia controlled interventions.

Clinical relevance

Myopia control practice is guided largely by RCT evidence, much of which involves industry participation. Variability in the transparency of COI disclosures may influence how such evidence is interpreted for clinical decision-making.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were systematically searched from inception to October 6, 2025. Eligible studies were RCTs of myopia controlled interventions in children or adolescents with at least 6 months of follow-up and reporting cycloplegic spherical equivalent and/or axial length outcomes. COI declaration transparency was categorized a priori into predefined levels. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Associations between COI transparency and study conclusions, statistical significance, and effect sizes were evaluated using cross-sectional, multiple meta-regression models. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261291949).

Results

A total of 134 RCTs were included. Sixteen trials (11.9%) did not report a COI statement, 85 (63.4%) provided simple declarations of no conflicts, 14 (10.4%) reported intermediate disclosures, and 19 (14.2%) provided detailed COI statements. Distributions of overall risk of bias and the domain of selective outcome reporting differed significantly across COI transparency categories, with a higher proportion of low-risk judgments observed in trials with more detailed COI disclosures (both P < .01). Overall, COI transparency was not significantly associated with study outcomes. However, in stratified analyses, greater COI transparency was significantly associated with more favorable study conclusions among trials evaluating optical interventions, even after adjustment for industry funding and other covariates (odds ratio = 2.66, 95% confidence interval: 1.19-5.92, P = .02). Similar patterns were observed in trials with larger sample sizes and those published in higher-impact factor journals, although these associations were attenuated after accounting for industry funding.

Conclusion

Transparency in COI declarations demonstrates context-specific relationships with study conclusions and reporting quality in myopia controlled trials. While transparent disclosure is essential for research integrity, its interpretation should be integrated with funding context when evaluating evidence to inform clinical practice.

records.title: Standardising ocular surface photography for artificial intelligence: current limitations and a proposed roadmap.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Standardising ocular surface photography for artificial intelligence: current limitations and a proposed roadmap.
content.abstract: Slit-lamp colour photography remains a cornerstone of anterior segment documentation and longitudinal monitoring. However, conventional slit-lamp photography has seen relatively limited technological advancement compared with the rapid development of quantitative anterior-segment modalities such as AS-OCT, Scheimpflug tomography and confocal microscopy. Despite the wide diffusion of digital cameras, smartphones, and high-end slit-lamp systems, ocular surface photography (OSP) remains hampered by the absence of standardised acquisition and processing protocols. The convex, aspheric geometry of the ocular surface, off-axis illumination, peripheral defocus, automatic colour correction, and pupil-driven exposure variation in retroillumination limit reproducibility, inter-device comparability, and clinical utility. In this review we critically appraise current OSP applications across major ocular surface conditions (dry eye disease, conjunctival hyperaemia, infectious keratitis, ocular surface burns, and ocular surface neoplasia), mapping the hardware, software, and reproducibility limitations that constrain clinical practice. We then examine how these limitations propagate into artificial intelligence (AI) development, where the absence of large, well-annotated, demographically diverse OSP datasets, together with the lack of reproducible quantitative phenotypes and reliable labels, is now the principal bottleneck to clinically deployable models; we discuss patient-level data partitioning and external validation, and outline how deep learning, federated learning and foundation models can both utilise and improve OSP. Finally, we propose a minimum acquisition and dataset specification, tiered by clinical setting from research to community screening, and a staged roadmap that combines hardware standardisation (focus-stacked, illumination-controlled, colour-calibrated acquisition), interoperable metadata-rich storage (DICOM where infrastructure permits), quantitative phenotype definition, and diverse international dataset collaborations, so that the ocular surface can benefit from quantitative imaging and AI as other areas of ophthalmology have begun to.

records.title: Efficacy of Thin and Ultrathin Descemet Stripping Automated Endothelial Keratoplasty and Influence of Graft Thickness on Postoperative Outcomes: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

content.title: Efficacy of Thin and Ultrathin Descemet Stripping Automated Endothelial Keratoplasty and Influence of Graft Thickness on Postoperative Outcomes: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis on the efficacy of thin and ultrathin Descemet stripping automated endothelial keratoplasty (T-DSAEK and UT-DSAEK, with graft thickness <130 and <100 µm, respectively), depending on graft thickness.

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis.

Method

PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase, ClinicalTrials.gov, and ScienceDirect databases were searched until October 1, 2021. We computed random-effect meta-analysis on postoperative outcomes of T/UT-DSAEK, stratified by graft thickness (<80 μm, 80-100 μm, and 100-130 μm). The main postoperative outcome was visual acuity (logarithm of the minimum angle of resolution [logMAR]). Secondary outcomes were pachymetry (μm), endothelial cell count (cell/mm2), spherical equivalent (diopter [D]), rebubbling rate (%), and rejection rate (%). Meta-regressions compared postoperative outcomes depending on graft thickness and search for putative confusion factors.

Results

We included 47 articles for a total of 2141 eyes of 2040 patients. T/UT-DSAEK globally improved visual acuity (effect size = -0.38 logMAR [95% confidence interval {CI} -0.46 to -0.30 logMAR]), without difference depending on graft thickness. Overall, pachymetry improved (-60.6 µm [95% CI -101 to -19.7 µm]), endothelial cell count decreased (-1039 cells/mm2 [95% CI -1209 to -868 cells/mm2), spherical equivalent resulted in a hyperopic shift (0.74 D [95% CI -0.50 to 1.97 D), the graft rejection rate was 0.2% (95% CI -0.1% to 0.4%), and the rebubbling rate was 8.7% (95% CI 6.8%-10.5%). Grafts >100 μm induced a hyperopic shift. Metaregressions did not demonstrate differences between the 3 groups (<80 μm, 80-100 μm, or 100-130 μm) in any outcomes.

Conclusion

All T/UT-DSAEK thickness groups provided similar visual acuity, pachymetry, endothelial cell count, rejection rate, and rebubbling rate regardless of graft thickness. A hyperopic shift was induced by grafts >100 μm.

records.title: Efficacy of Amniotic Membrane Grafting for the Treatment of Chemical and Thermal Ocular Surface Injuries: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology.

content.title: Efficacy of Amniotic Membrane Grafting for the Treatment of Chemical and Thermal Ocular Surface Injuries: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology.
content.abstract:
Objective

To evaluate the published literature on the efficacy of amniotic membrane grafting (AMG) in the management of acute chemical and thermal ocular surface burns with respect to the rate of corneal re-epithelialization and improvement of visual acuity or corneal clarity.

Methods

Literature searches were conducted in the PubMed database in May 2023 and updated in January 2024 and were limited to the English language without date restrictions. The searches yielded 474 citations; 58 were reviewed in full text, and 9 met the inclusion criteria. Four studies were rated level II, and 5 studies were rated level III. This assessment focuses on 3 level II articles that provided consistent primary and secondary outcomes but demonstrated suboptimal study design with respect to power calculations and lacked a priori sample-size calculations.

Results

Amniotic membrane grafting significantly improved corneal re-epithelialization compared with medical therapy alone in eyes with moderate-grade burns. For severely burned eyes, AMG demonstrated no advantage over medical therapy. Additionally, AMG demonstrated no significant advantage over medical therapy for improved visual acuity or corneal clarity for moderate or severe ocular surface burns.

Conclusions

The best available level II evidence suggests that AMG in the setting of acute ocular surface burns has efficacy in hastening re-epithelialization in moderate burns. As an adjuvant to medical therapy, it did not demonstrate a benefit in improving re-epithelialization in severe burns or visual acuity or corneal clarity in either moderate or severe burns.

Financial disclosure(s)

Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found after the references.

records.title: Unravelling CYP4V2: Clinical features, genetic insights, pathogenic mechanisms and therapeutic strategies in Bietti crystalline corneoretinal dystrophy.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Unravelling CYP4V2: Clinical features, genetic insights, pathogenic mechanisms and therapeutic strategies in Bietti crystalline corneoretinal dystrophy.
content.abstract: Inherited retinal dystrophies (IRDs) comprise a spectrum of disease phenotypes with genetic heterogeneity and clinical phenotypic diversity. Bietti crystalline corneoretinal dystrophy (BCD) represents a distinct IRD subtype characterized by crystalline deposits in the retina. Although rare in Western populations, BCD ranks among the most prevalent IRDs in East Asia, affecting an estimated 124,000 to 377,000 individuals worldwide. As a severe type of IRD, BCD demonstrates accelerated progression and currently lacks effective treatment. The BCD disease is caused by a biallelic mutation in the CYP4V2 gene. With a coding sequence (CDS) of 1,578 bp, CYP4V2 can be effectively encapsulated into adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors. As a hydroxylase, CYP4V2 is mainly expressed in retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) cells, which can be transduced by AAVs and are suitable for gene augmentation therapy that replaces the function of mutant proteins. Given the large patient population, severe visual impairment, and feasibility of gene therapy, several research groups are interested in developing gene therapy products for BCD, and two products entering Phase III clinical trials have made significant progress. This review outlines the clinical features, genetic insights and pathogenic mechanisms of BCD and discusses the ongoing gene therapy clinical trials, including efficacy and concerns. This knowledge will help us bridge the gap between molecular studies and clinical treatments, facilitating translation from bench to bedside. We believe that advancements in BCD gene therapy will inform the treatment of other IRDs.

records.title: Investing in vision: Innovation in retinal therapeutics and the influence on venture capital investment.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Investing in vision: Innovation in retinal therapeutics and the influence on venture capital investment.
content.abstract: Since the groundbreaking approval of the first anti-VEGF therapy in 2004, the retinal therapeutics field has undergone a remarkable transformation, witnessing a surge in novel, disease-modifying therapeutics for a broad spectrum of retinal diseases, extending beyond exudative VEGF-driven conditions. The surge in scientific advancement and the pressing, unmet, medical need have captured the attention of venture capital investors, who have collectively invested close to $10 billion in research and development of new retinal therapeutics between 2004 and 2023. Notably, the field of exudative diseases has gradually shifted away from trying to outcompete anti-VEGF therapeutics towards lowering the overall treatment burden by reducing injection frequency. Simultaneously, a new era has emerged in the non-exudative field, targeting prevalent conditions like dry AMD and rare indications such as Retinitis pigmentosa. This has led to promising drug candidates in development, culminating in the landmark approval of Luxturna for a rare form of Retinitis pigmentosa. The validation of new mechanisms, such as the complement pathway in dry AMD has paved the way for the approvals of Syvovre (Apellis) and Izervay (Iveric/Astellas), marking the first two therapies for this condition. In this comprehensive review, we share our view on the cumulative lessons from the past two decades in developing retinal therapeutics, covering both positive achievements and challenges. We also contextualize the investments, strategic partnering deals, and acquisitions of biotech companies, pharmaceutical companies venture capital investors in retinal therapeutics, respectively. Finally, we provide an outlook and potentially a forward-looking roadmap on novel retinal therapeutics, highlighting the emergence of potential new intervention strategies, such as cell-based therapies, gene editing, and combination therapies. We conclude that upcoming developments have the potential to further stimulate venture capital investments, which ultimately could facilitate the development and delivery of new therapies to patients in need.

records.title: Updated Guidelines for Imaging the Choriocapillaris in Eyes with Age-Related Macular Degeneration Using Swept-Source Optical Coherence Tomography Angiography.

content.title: Updated Guidelines for Imaging the Choriocapillaris in Eyes with Age-Related Macular Degeneration Using Swept-Source Optical Coherence Tomography Angiography.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To update the recommended guidelines when quantifying choriocapillaris (CC) flow deficits (FDs) in eyes with age-related macular degeneration (AMD) using swept-source optical coherence tomography angiography (SS-OCTA).

Design

Evidence-based perspective.

Methods

Review of literature and experience of authors.

Results

A current challenge when quantifying CC FDs using SS-OCTA is the implementation of an objective compensation strategy to adjust for the signal attenuation arising under drusen in eyes with AMD. Our previous compensation strategy was used as a general approach to adjust for the OCTA signal attenuation associated with most drusen. However, the variability of the OCTA signal loss under drusen necessitated a more objective strategy that could be tailored to each case. We propose a compensation strategy using a parameter gamma (γ) that allows for the selection of an appropriate compensation level. The optimal γ value is identified as the one producing the most homogeneous OCT signal across the whole CC structural slab. This approach minimizes the possibility that areas of decreased flow in the compensated CC flow image might reflect drusen-related or compensation-related artifacts rather than true deficits. Additional lesions that present unique challenges when quantifying CC FDs include the presence of choroidal hypotransmission defects (hypoTDs) caused by calcified drusen and hyperreflective foci as well as choroidal hypertransmission defects (hyperTDs) caused by foci of atrophy. We recommend identifying and outlining these regions on an en face sub-retinal pigment epithelium (subRPE) slab with segmentation boundaries between 64 and 400 µm beneath the Bruch membrane (BM). The hypoTDs should be excluded from CC quantification because of the lack of significant OCTA signal, whereas the hyperTDs should be excluded from being compensated because doing so can artifactually increase the percentage of CC FDs.

Conclusions

The analysis of CC FDs in AMD requires special attention to drusen, hypoTDs, and hyperTDs to avoid introducing artifacts. By properly adjusting the compensation levels under drusen and adjusting the quantification of CC FDs by accounting for hyperTDs and hypoTDs, researchers interested in measuring CC FDs in AMD can have greater confidence in their measurements, particularly when investigating the role of CC flow impairment in AMD progression.

records.title: Impact of Vision Impairment and Ocular Morbidity and Their Treatment on Depression and Anxiety in Children: A Systematic Review.

content.title: Impact of Vision Impairment and Ocular Morbidity and Their Treatment on Depression and Anxiety in Children: A Systematic Review.
content.abstract:
Topic

This systematic review and meta-analysis summarizes existing evidence to establish whether vision impairment, ocular morbidity, and their treatment are associated with depression and anxiety in children.

Clinical relevance

Understanding and quantifying these associations support early detection and management of mental health symptoms in children with vision impairment and ocular morbidity. Additionally, this review provides evidence in favor of insurance coverage for timely strabismus surgery.

Methods

We searched 9 electronic databases from inception through February 18, 2021, including observational and interventional studies assessing whether vision impairment, ocular morbidity, or both and their treatment are associated with depression, anxiety, or both in children. We used narrative synthesis and meta-analysis with the residual maximum likelihood method. A protocol was registered and published on The International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (identifier: CRD42021233323).

Results

Among 28 992 studies, 28 956 studies (99.9%) were excluded as duplicates or unrelated content. Among 36 remaining studies, 21 studies (58.3%) were observational studies concerning vision impairment, 8 studies (22.2%) were observational studies concerning strabismus, and 7 studies (19.4%) were interventional studies. Vision impaired children demonstrated significantly higher scores of depression (standard mean difference [SMD], 0.57; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.26-0.89; 11 studies) and anxiety (SMD, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.40-0.83; 14 studies) than normally sighted children. In particular, children with myopia demonstrated higher scores of depression (SMD, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.36-0.81; 6 studies) than normally sighted children. Strabismus surgery significantly improved symptoms of depression (SMD, 0.59; 95% CI, 0.12-1.06; 3 studies) and anxiety (SMD, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.25-1.14; 4 studies) in children.

Conclusion

Among children, vision impairment is associated with greater symptoms of depression and anxiety. Surgical treatment of strabismus improved these symptoms. Further randomized controlled trials exploring the impact of public health measures for myopia correction on mental health in children are needed. Scaling up access to strabismus surgery could improve the mental health of affected children.

records.title: Optical coherence tomography in the management of diabetic macular oedema.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Optical coherence tomography in the management of diabetic macular oedema.
content.abstract: Diabetic macular oedema (DMO) is the major cause of visual impairment in people with diabetes. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) is now the most widely used modality to assess presence and severity of DMO. DMO is currently broadly classified based on the involvement to the central 1 mm of the macula into non-centre or centre involved DMO (CI-DMO) and DMO can occur with or without visual acuity (VA) loss. This classification forms the basis of management strategies of DMO. Despite years of research on quantitative and qualitative DMO related features assessed by OCT, these do not fully inform physicians of the prognosis and severity of DMO relative to visual function. Having said that, recent research on novel OCT biomarkers development and re-defined classification of DMO show better correlation with visual function and treatment response. This review summarises the current evidence of the association of OCT biomarkers in DMO management and its potential clinical importance in predicting VA and anatomical treatment response. The review also discusses some future directions in this field, such as the use of artificial intelligence to quantify and monitor OCT biomarkers and retinal fluid and identify phenotypes of DMO, and the need for standardisation and classification of OCT biomarkers to use in future clinical trials and clinical practice settings as prognostic markers and secondary treatment outcome measures in the management of DMO.

records.title: Deep Learning Model for Image-Based Classification of Four Keratitis Categories.

content.title: Deep Learning Model for Image-Based Classification of Four Keratitis Categories.
content.abstract:
Purpose

CorneAI was developed to classify anterior segment conditions into 9 categories. We aimed to develop a deep learning (DL) model for image-based classification among 4 selected keratitis categories: catarrhal ulcer, herpes stromal keratitis, peripheral ulcerative keratitis (PUK), and phlyctenular keratitis.

Methods

We retrospectively collected 973 anterior segment images from 576 patients at 7 institutions in Japan and the Japan Ocular Imaging Registry. A YOLOv5 model was developed and evaluated using five-fold cross-validation. In an exploratory analysis, 17 ophthalmologists classified 192 images from 1 randomly selected validation fold.

Results

The positive predictive values (95% confidence interval) were 0.72 (0.59-0.83) for catarrhal ulcer, 0.84 (0.77-0.89) for herpes stromal keratitis, 0.88 (0.85-0.91) for PUK, and 0.72 (0.65-0.77) for phlyctenular keratitis. The areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves were 0.81 (0.74-0.87), 0.90 (0.87-0.93), 0.94 (0.93-0.96), and 0.91 (0.88-0.93), respectively. Sensitivity and specificity were 0.47 (0.37-0.58) and 0.98 (0.97-0.99) for catarrhal ulcer, 0.72 (0.65-0.79) and 0.97 (0.95-0.98) for herpes stromal keratitis, 0.93 (0.91-0.95) and 0.87 (0.84-0.90) for PUK, and 0.81 (0.75-0.86) and 0.91 (0.89-0.93) for phlyctenular keratitis. In an exploratory analysis, the diagnostic accuracies were 76.6% (95% CI, 70.1%-82.0%) for YOLOv5, 72.5 ± 9.3% (range, 53.6%-80.2%; n = 7) for corneal specialists, and 64.5 ± 10.2% (range, 45.3%-78.1%; n = 10) for ophthalmology residents.

Conclusions

We developed a DL model for image-based classification among 4 selected keratitis categories. Further validation in broader clinical populations, including other corneal diseases and normal corneas, is required before clinical application.

records.title: The association between large language model dependence and academic anxiety among nursing students: statistical indirect associations through artificial intelligence addiction and academic burnout.

content.title: The association between large language model dependence and academic anxiety among nursing students: statistical indirect associations through artificial intelligence addiction and academic burnout.
content.abstract:
Background

Increasing use of large language models in nursing education has raised questions about the association between reliance on these tools and academic distress. This study examined direct and specific indirect associations between large language model dependence (LMD) and academic anxiety (AA) through artificial intelligence addiction (AIA) and academic burnout (AB).

Methods

A cross-sectional survey was conducted from March to April 2026 among 473 nursing students in Guangdong Province, China, including students undertaking clinical placements. The four constructs were assessed using items selected from published self-report instruments. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was performed with age and sex included as covariates. Direct and specific indirect associations were evaluated using bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples.

Results

Cronbach's α ranged from 0.914 to 0.944, composite reliability from 0.935 to 0.954, and average variance extracted from 0.560 to 0.721. Heterotrait-monotrait ratios ranged from 0.485 to 0.733, supporting discriminant validity. Model fit evidence was mixed: SRMR was 0.068, whereas NFI was 0.812, below the 0.90 reference value. The model explained 49.2% of the variance in academic anxiety. Large language model dependence showed a small positive direct association with academic anxiety (β = 0.138, 95% CI [0.006, 0.278], p = 0.048). Significant specific indirect associations were identified through academic burnout (β = 0.205, 95% CI [0.123, 0.303]) and through artificial intelligence addiction followed by academic burnout (β = 0.098, 95% CI [0.049, 0.147]); both p < 0.001.

Conclusion

Large language model dependence was positively associated with academic anxiety among nursing students, with specific indirect associations through academic burnout and through artificial intelligence addiction followed by academic burnout. These findings highlight the relevance of problematic AI use and study-related exhaustion to academic distress. However, the cross-sectional design does not establish temporal ordering or causal mediation.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in odontology education.

content.title: Artificial intelligence in odontology education.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored in dental education as a tool to support teaching, learning, assessment, and clinical decision-making. This systematic review synthesized current evidence on the implementation and educational impact of AI technologies in undergraduate, postgraduate, and continuing dental education.

Methodology

A PRISMA-guided systematic review was conducted using Scopus, PubMed, and IEEE Xplore. Studies published between 2020 and 2025 evaluating AI applications in dental education were identified using predefined PICO criteria. Educational outcomes included knowledge acquisition, diagnostic accuracy, clinical reasoning, procedural skills, learner engagement, and perceptions of AI-assisted learning.

Results

The included literature reflects an expansion from machine learning, deep learning, and computer vision systems primarily evaluated for diagnostic support toward generative AI platforms, including large language models and retrieval-augmented generation systems. Across the included studies, AI applications were frequently associated with favorable diagnostic and examination performance and, in selected educational contexts, with supportive findings related to clinical reasoning, technical competency, feedback, and self-directed learning. However, the evidence was predominantly based on technical performance assessments and observational or cross-sectional designs.

Discussion

AI is increasingly being explored as a potential complementary educational resource, with applications including interactive tutoring, adaptive learning, and support for clinical reasoning. Nevertheless, heterogeneous methodologies and limited longitudinal evidence indicate the need for standardized educational evaluation and responsible curricular integration.

Conclusion

AI shows potential as a complementary resource in dental education. Its integration should remain pedagogically guided and ethically supervised while future research establishes its educational effectiveness through standardized and longitudinal evaluation.

records.title: One step beyond CASA Systems: Artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning (DL) for canine sperm analysis (CSA).

content.title: One step beyond CASA Systems: Artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning (DL) for canine sperm analysis (CSA).
content.abstract: Computer Assisted Sperm Analysis (CASA) systems have become indispensable tools for determinining objective motility (percentage) and precise kinematic parameters (velocities μm/sec) in mammalian semen analysis over the past decades. However, conventional CASA platforms dependent on grayscale image acquisition and predefined mathematical algorithms. These rigid frameworks are often inadequate for capturing the complex, dynamic movement patterns of spermatozoa. In canine reproduction, where semen quality asssessment critical for Breeding Soundness Examinations (BSEs), Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART), and clinical decision making, these limitations may compromise the accuracy and clinical relevance of motility based diagnostics. Recent advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Deep Learning (DL) offer transformative opportunities to overcome the intrinsic constraints of conventional CASA systems. AI/DL based approaches enable data driven feature extraction, improved sperm detection and superior tracking capabilities. Unlike traditional CASAs, AI/DL integrated systems, having been recently developed provide robust classification of motility patterns without strict dependence on manually defined thresholds, reducing sensitivity to variables such as illumination, magnification and background extender and seminal plasma (SP) or spermatogenesis based particiles. Moreover, DL models can simultaneously integrate spatial, temporal and morphological information as specialized datasets expand. This article summarized the current state of the art in conventional (gray scale) and modern (AI/DL) canine CASA applications and critically discusses their methodological limitations based on studies published between 2013 and 2026, also covering researches and development pathway related with three successive projects: ESAS (2014-2018)_conventional/ESAS TİP (2018-2022)_AI-DL and ESAS TÜG_AI-DL (initiated 2022 and in progress) partly financially and scientifically supported by The Scientific and Technological Research Council of Türkiye (TÜBİTAK) and Technology and Innovation Funding Programmes Directorate (TEYDEB) (2013-2018 conventional, 2018-2026 AI/DL model R&D studies, especially 1507 and TÜBİTAK TEYDEB 1501 R&D Program (ESAS Commercial Product Development (TÜG) Project No: 3230063)). This current article highlights the technological transition from fragmented, parameter based motility assessments toward holistic, pattern oriented sperm evaluations, evaluating its ultimate implications for fertility prediction and routine canine veterinary andrology with one step beyond of conventional CASA with deep learning and artificial intelligence.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in glaucoma diagnosis and management: a systematic review of the past decade (2015-2026).

content.title: Artificial intelligence in glaucoma diagnosis and management: a systematic review of the past decade (2015-2026).
content.abstract:
Introduction

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being used to support glaucoma detection and monitoring, with rapid advances in deep learning, multimodal imaging, and longitudinal prediction. This review evaluates the evidence supporting these developments and identifies barriers to clinical translation.

Areas covered

A systematic search of PubMed, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, and SpringerLink was conducted following PRISMA guidelines, with the protocol registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261450819). Of 3,758 records identified, 63 eligible peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2026 were included. The review examined AI techniques, imaging modalities, datasets, diagnostic and predictive performance, validation strategies, and reported limitations in Glaucoma care. Most studies used deep learning applied to fundus photography, optical coherence tomography (OCT), OCT angiography, visual fields, or multimodal data. Many models achieved an area under the ROC curve of approximately 0.95.

Expert opinion

AI has substantial potential to improve glaucoma detection and monitoring, but high reported accuracy alone does not establish clinical readiness. Prospective multicenter validation using diverse populations, explainable and reproducible models, standardized evaluation, and integration into clinical workflows are essential before widespread implementation.

records.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.

content.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Echocardiography has evolved substantially since its introduction in 1954. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers transformative potential for image acquisition, quantification, interpretation, and reporting. Despite growing research interest, a comprehensive evaluation of the historical trends and evolution of AI in echocardiography is lacking. The study aimed to conduct a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of the global research landscape in this field.

Methods

A systematic literature search was conducted using the Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection databases for publications on AI in echocardiography from inception through November 10, 2025; no language filter was applied. Data analysis was performed using Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Access, and IBM SPSS Statistics. In addition, bibliometric mapping and data visualization were conducted.

Results

Overall, 2682 publications received 35,083 citations (mean, 13.08 citations per publication), spanning 1984-2025. Original articles, conference papers, and review articles accounted for 87.4% and 98.5% of total publications and citations, respectively. Publication output remained limited until approximately 2015, rose gradually thereafter, and accelerated markedly after 2018, with similar output in 2024 and 2025. The United States led in both publication volume and total citations, followed by China and the United Kingdom. The United States also had the highest collaboration link strength, and seven of the top 10 institutions were in North America (six in the United States and one in Canada). Mayo Clinic ranked first, with 142 publications and 3604 citations, and had the earliest first indexed publication among the top institutions (1992). The journal JACC: Cardiovascular Imaging ranked first in both total citations (1,911) and citations per publication (36.75). "Echocardiography," "deep learning," "artificial intelligence," and "machine learning" were the most frequently used terms. The thematic evolution showed continuity of algorithmic-centric themes (1984-2019) with emerging clinically oriented themes (2020-2025).

Conclusions

This comprehensive bibliometric analysis highlights the rapid expansion of AI research in echocardiography, characterized by an accelerating publication output and emerging clinically oriented research topics. These findings reflect growing research interest in integrating AI into echocardiographic practice and highlight the need for future research prioritizing multicenter validation, clinical translation, and equitable real-world implementation.

records.title: Artificial intelligence analysis of oral mucosal lesions in white-light clinical photographs: A systematic review of visual features and validation.

content.title: Artificial intelligence analysis of oral mucosal lesions in white-light clinical photographs: A systematic review of visual features and validation.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to conventional oral photographs for recognition, classification, localization, segmentation, and risk assessment of oral mucosal lesions. This systematic review evaluated how clinically relevant visual information-including color, texture, morphology, borders, and spatial patterns-is represented by AI systems and assessed performance, validation, explainability, human comparison, and clinical translation. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for studies directly analyzing conventional white-light clinical photographs. Risk of bias was assessed with PROBAST + AI, and certainty with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation-based approaches. Fifty-three studies were included, 30 published in 2025-2026. Forty-six used implicit deep-learning visual representations, three multimodal vision-language models, two explicit color analyses, and two explicit texture analyses. Thirty-one studies primarily addressed image-level diagnostic classification/recognition, 15 spatial detection/localization or lesion delineation, six screening/triage/referral or biopsy-oriented decision support, and one longitudinal malignant-transformation prediction. Six used independent external cohorts and five compared AI with human readers. Methodological concerns were frequent, no sufficiently coherent group supported meta-analysis, and certainty remained limited across evidence bodies. Current evidence therefore supports technical feasibility rather than established clinical effectiveness, with translation requiring stronger patient-level independence, external validation, prospective multicenter evaluation, and evidence of clinical benefit.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in the in vitro fertilization laboratory: A scoping review and SWOT-based evaluation of emerging applications.

content.title: Artificial intelligence in the in vitro fertilization laboratory: A scoping review and SWOT-based evaluation of emerging applications.
content.abstract:
Objective

Artificial intelligence (AI) represents a potentially transformative tool in assisted reproductive technology (ART), particularly in vitro fertilization (IVF), for gamete assessment, embryo selection, non-invasive genetic testing, and laboratory automation. This scoping review synthesized recent evidence on AI applications in IVF laboratories and evaluated their translational maturity using an evidence maturity framework and a strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats (SWOT) analysis.

Methods

This scoping review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) Extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for peer-reviewed studies published from January 2020 to February 2025. Eligible studies evaluated AI, machine learning, or deep learning in laboratory components of ART. Data were charted on AI methods, dataset characteristics, validation strategies, clinical endpoints, and performance metrics.

Results

Ninety-four studies were included. Most applications addressed embryo grading and implantation prediction using convolutional neural networks and were evaluated through internal cross-validation. Reported areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve ranged from 0.75 to 0.92, depending on the endpoint and dataset size. AI applications in sperm analysis and oocyte assessment showed greater reproducibility than manual evaluation. Non-invasive genetic prediction models displayed promising but heterogeneous sensitivity and remained predominantly limited to internal validation. Few studies reported prospective evaluation or external validation using multicenter datasets.

Conclusion

AI applications in IVF are expanding, but most remain at early stages of clinical translation. Standardized datasets, external validation, interpretable algorithms, and regulatory oversight remain necessary for safe, equitable clinical integration. AI should function as a decision-support tool that supplements, rather than replaces, embryologists' expertise.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence Methods in Stroke Prediction: A Narrative Review.
records.publisher: Annals of Indian Academy of Neurology

content.title: Artificial Intelligence Methods in Stroke Prediction: A Narrative Review.
content.abstract:
Abstract

Stroke is a leading cause of mortality worldwide. Despite rising healthcare costs, early noninvasive stroke risk stratification via artificial intelligence provides accurate, rapid predictions, establishing AI as a powerful tool in healthcare by enabling tailored treatment for stroke patients. Traditional algorithms assess risk using regression-based statistical correlations, which, while practical and user-friendly, show moderate predictive accuracy. Machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models effectively identify individuals at higher risk of stroke across diverse populations, enabling timely intervention. However, evidence summarizing the effectiveness of these approaches remains sparse. This review presents various ML and DL algorithms, clarifying their theoretical foundations, historical evolution, and applications in stroke prediction. This narrative review focuses on studies published within the last five years and emphasizes the clinical relevance and translational potential of AI-based stroke prediction models.

records.title: Direct randomized evidence for systemic targeted therapies in prurigo nodularis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Direct randomized evidence for systemic targeted therapies in prurigo nodularis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Systemic targeted therapies are reshaping treatment for prurigo nodularis (PN), but the timing of clinically meaningful benefits and the strength of supporting evidence remain unclear. We synthesized direct placebo-controlled evidence by outcome and follow-up time, distinguishing replicated phase 3 evidence from preliminary signals.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception to June 30, 2026, for randomized controlled trials of systemic targeted therapies for PN. Compatible outcomes were pooled separately at prespecified time points using random-effects models. The primary outcome was a ≥ 4-point reduction in weekly average Worst Itch or Peak Pruritus Numerical Rating Scale scores. Secondary outcomes included Investigator's Global Assessment (IGA) success, dual response, sleep, quality of life, psychological outcomes, and safety. Risk of bias and certainty were assessed using RoB 2 and GRADE.

Results

Eleven trials involving 1,623 participants evaluated six therapies. Itch response favored active treatment at weeks 4 (RR 4.76, 95% CI 3.01-7.55), 12 (2.67, 1.43-5.00), 16 (3.32, 2.57-4.29), and 24 (3.09, 2.18-4.38), whereas the week 8 estimate was imprecise (1.73, 0.94-3.21). IGA success was supported from week 8 onward. Nemolizumab improved sleep response by week 4, and two phase 3 dupilumab trials showed a week 24 dual-response benefit (RR 3.98, 2.31-6.85). Treatment-emergent adverse events were modestly more frequent with active treatment (RR 1.14, 1.06-1.24), while serious adverse events and discontinuations did not clearly increase. The most robust evidence came from replicated phase 3 programs of dupilumab and nemolizumab.

Conclusion

Replicated randomized evidence supports clinically meaningful improvements in itch and lesion outcomes with dupilumab and nemolizumab. Symptomatic benefits may emerge earlier than lesion responses, but this pattern should be interpreted cautiously because evidence across time points derives from limited, partly non-overlapping trial sets. Comparative treatment ranking is not supported, and longer-term data are needed to define rare, delayed, and agent-specific harms.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?ID=CRD420261445753, identifier CRD420261445753.

records.title: Heart failure and suicide mortality and suicide attempts: a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies.

content.title: Heart failure and suicide mortality and suicide attempts: a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies.
content.abstract:
Objective

This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to synthesize longitudinal observational evidence on the associations of heart failure (HF) with suicide mortality and suicide attempts.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched from inception to April 11, 2026, to identify cohort studies evaluating suicide mortality or suicide attempts among individuals with HF. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Because suicide mortality and suicide attempts are clinically distinct outcomes, they were analyzed separately. The primary quantitative synthesis was restricted to studies evaluating suicide death or completed suicide and reporting adjusted hazard ratios (HRs). Adjusted HRs were log-transformed and pooled using a generic inverse-variance random-effects model. Studies evaluating suicide attempts were summarized narratively because only two studies were available and they differed substantially in population, clinical setting, and effect measure. Between-study heterogeneity was assessed using Cochran's Q test and the I² statistic.

Results

Seven cohort studies published between 2018 and 2026, involving 17,696,608 participants, were included in the systematic review. Five studies evaluating suicide death or completed suicide contributed to the primary meta-analysis. HF was associated with suicide mortality, with a pooled adjusted HR of [HR] (95% CI: [lower-upper]; I2 = [I2]%, P for heterogeneity = [P value]). Two studies evaluated suicide attempts but were not pooled because one reported an HR in a large community-based cohort, whereas the other reported an RR in a small, highly selected population of patients with end-stage HF undergoing left ventricular assist device implantation. No included study reported suicidal ideation as an independently extractable longitudinal outcome.

Conclusion

Observational cohort evidence suggests that HF is associated with an increased hazard of suicide mortality. Evidence regarding suicide attempts remains too limited and heterogeneous for a reliable pooled estimate, and no independently extractable longitudinal evidence was available for suicidal ideation. Residual confounding, between-study heterogeneity, and the small number of eligible studies limit causal interpretation and the certainty of the findings.

records.title: Strategies and tools for enhancing early detection of pancreatic cancer.
records.publisher: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association = Taiwan yi zhi

content.title: Strategies and tools for enhancing early detection of pancreatic cancer.
content.abstract: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PAC) remains the most lethal malignancies, with a 5-year survival rate of only around 12%. The dismal prognosis is largely attributable to late diagnosis, as early PAC is frequently asymptomatic and radiologically inconspicuous. Contemporary international guidelines recommend surveillance for well-defined high-risk groups, particularly carriers of pathogenic germline mutations such as BRCA2, STK11, and CDKN2A, as well as familial pancreatic cancer kindreds. In these settings, endoscopic ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging are the recommended surveillance modalities. Recent advances in biomarker discovery, including circulating tumor DNA, methylation signatures of cell-free DNA, and extracellular vesicles, have demonstrated encouraging results, particularly when combined with CA19-9. Paraneoplastic phenomena such as pancreatic cancer-associated diabetes and cancer-induced cachexia provide additional opportunities for earlier clinical recognition. Parallel progress has been achieved in artificial intelligence-driven radiomics analysis and deep learning algorithms, which can increase the sensitivity of cross-sectional imaging for small or otherwise occult lesions. The integration of clinical risk stratification, molecular biomarkers, and AI-enhanced imaging represents a promising framework to shift diagnosis toward surgically resectable stages. This review synthesizes the current evidence, highlights recent advances, and discusses practical considerations for physicians to facilitate earlier detection of PAC.

records.title: Artificial intelligence and machine learning in heart and lung transplantation.

content.title: Artificial intelligence and machine learning in heart and lung transplantation.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are increasingly applied across the heart and lung transplant continuum, from donor organ evaluation and waitlist prioritisation through peri-operative decision support to post-transplant rejection surveillance and personalised immunosuppression. Deep learning for endomyocardial biopsy interpretation has achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.962, with performance comparable to expert pathologists, while ML-augmented ex-vivo lung perfusion platforms have demonstrated the potential to expand organ utilisation in real-world implementation studies. Noninvasive donor-derived cell-free DNA assays and electrocardiogram-based deep learning models are beginning to reduce dependence on invasive surveillance biopsies. Across published studies, models predicting 1-year post-transplant mortality have shown only moderate discrimination. Most published models remain retrospectively validated on single-centre datasets with limited external validation, inconsistent calibration reporting, and unresolved concerns about algorithmic bias and global health equity. This scoping review synthesises current evidence, critically appraises model performance, and identifies the regulatory, ethical, and methodological steps required for responsible clinical integration. Future research should prioritise prospective, multicentre external validation, transparent calibration reporting, and formal evaluation of clinical utility before these tools are adopted in routine transplant care.

records.title: Health economics evaluation of artificial intelligence in the field of oncology: a scoping review.

content.title: Health economics evaluation of artificial intelligence in the field of oncology: a scoping review.
content.abstract: BACKGROUND: The ageing and growing population, rising cancer rate, and increased healthcare demand drive higher medical costs. Integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) into oncology revolutionizes cancer diagnosis, treatment, and management, promising enhanced efficiency and precision. Despite potential for healthcare cost savings from implementing AI system in healthcare, its successful integration depends on stakeholder acceptance, particularly physician adoption and integration into routine clinical practice. OBJECTIVES: This scoping review aimed to systematically assess recent literature on health economic evaluations (HEEs) of artificial AI applications in oncology and explore the economic risks and benefits of integrating AI systems into oncology. METHODOLOGY: A scoping review was conducted using PRISMA-ScR guidelines across databases, including PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar for articles published between January 1, 2019, and June 30, 2024, in English. Eligible studies focused on the economic aspects of AI applications in oncology, including cost-effectiveness analyses, budget impact studies, and evaluations of economic benefits in clinical practice. Two independent reviewers used CHEERS-AI and Philips checklists for data extraction, quality assessment and analysis. RESULTS: Out of 870 studies identified,12 studies were selected which focused on colorectal (5), breast (2), lung (2), cervical (1), and prostate (1) cancers. Most emphasis is on early-stage care (N = 10,83%) and cost-effectiveness analysis (N = 9,75%) was predominant along with Markov model being the most common approach. The studies used a healthcare system perspective (N = 6,50%) and examined AI's cost-effectiveness in medical imaging (N = 5,42%) and biomarkers (N = 4,33%). Time horizons varied from less than a year to a lifetime, with most applying a 3% discount rate. AI demonstrated economic benefits, improved diagnostic sensitivity,potential cost reduction, workflow efficiency, and treatment optimization while presenting risks like reimbursement challenges, data security concerns, and potential error costs. CONCLUSION: The scoping review highlights the necessity for thorough health economic evaluations of AI integration in oncology. Although AI technologies are cost-effective, there is a gap in user perspectives and considerations of health equity, regulation, and ethics. To maximize its benefits, future research should include a comprehensive economic evaluation of a more diverse population for the effective adoption of AI into the healthcare system.

records.title: Application of AI in Hypertension Health Education: Scoping Review.

content.title: Application of AI in Hypertension Health Education: Scoping Review.
content.abstract:
Background

Hypertension is a major global health challenge, and effective health education is crucial for improving patients' self-management. Traditional health education approaches are often limited by insufficient personalization, accessibility, and scalability. Artificial intelligence (AI), including natural language processing, machine learning, and large language models (LLMs), offers promising solutions to address these limitations. However, evidence regarding AI applications in hypertension health education has not been comprehensively synthesized.

Objective

This scoping review aimed to summarize the current evidence on AI applications in hypertension health education, and identify research gaps to inform future research and practice.

Methods

This review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews) guidelines. Six databases (PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, and Scopus) were searched from January 2015 to June 2026. Eligibility criteria were developed using the participant-concept-context framework. Two reviewers independently conducted study screening and data extraction. Study designs were classified using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool framework. Consistent with scoping review methodology, no formal quality assessment was performed. Findings were synthesized narratively and presented using evidence gap maps, tables, and figures.

Results

A total of 24 studies from 11 countries were included, comprising 6 randomized controlled trials, 4 nonrandomized trials, 11 quantitative descriptive studies, and 3 mixed methods studies. Most studies were published between 2024 and 2026. In total, 3 AI application scenarios were identified: rule-based health education, data-driven adaptive health education, and generative AI-driven health education. Natural language processing was the most widely applied technology, and LLM-based applications increased rapidly after 2023. However, generative AI studies were predominantly proof-of-concept evaluations and lacked randomized clinical validation. Health education was rarely implemented as a standalone intervention and was typically embedded within multifunctional AI platforms. Outcomes were categorized using the Digital Health Scorecard Framework across 4 domains: technology, clinical, usability, and cost. Technical accuracy and blood pressure outcomes were the most frequently reported measures, whereas no study evaluated economic outcomes.

Conclusions

This first scoping review of AI applications in hypertension health education identified a mismatch between rapid advances in generative AI and the limited availability of rigorous clinical evidence. Three major research gaps were identified: (1) the lack of standardized core outcome sets covering technical, behavioral, clinical, and implementation domains; (2) limited development of hybrid architectures integrating LLM with structured medical knowledge bases; and (3) the absence of evaluation frameworks that satisfy both regulatory and implementation requirements. AI appears most suitable as a complement to, rather than a replacement for, clinician-delivered education. Future research should prioritize rigorous clinical validation, economic evaluation, multicultural adaptation, and health literacy equity to ensure that AI-driven health education reduces rather than exacerbates disparities in hypertension control.

records.title: DIAGNOSTIC PERFORMANCE OF MACHINE LEARNING-AIDED PROXIMAL CARIES DETECTION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS.
records.publisher: The journal of evidence-based dental practice

content.title: DIAGNOSTIC PERFORMANCE OF MACHINE LEARNING-AIDED PROXIMAL CARIES DETECTION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS.
content.abstract:
Objectives

The systematic review aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of machine learning in detecting proximal caries through radiographic modalities compared to expert consensus.

Materials and methods

A strategic literature search was carried out across 4 electronic databases, with 2 independent reviewers for screening and data extraction. Measures as sensitivity, specificity, positive (LR+) and negative likelihood ratios (LR-), area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) and diagnostic odds ratio (DOR) were calculated. Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality Assessment tool for Diagnostic Accuracy Studies (QUADAS-2). Subgroup analysis was performed based on the data modalities and image augmentation. The certainty of evidence was evaluated according to the Grading of Recommendation, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) framework.

Results

Following a thorough review of 2439 studies, 28 studies met the inclusion criteria. Eleven studies were included in the meta-analysis. The pooled sensitivity and specificity were 0.84 (95% Confidence Interval [95% CI] 0.78-0.88) and 0.93 (95% CI 0.90-0.97) respectively. The LR+ and LR- were 14.00 (95% CI 8.30-23.40) and 0.17 (95% CI 0.12-0.23) respectively. The pooled AUC-ROC was 0.95 (95% CI 0.17-1.00), and DOR was 84.08 (95% CI 40.54-174.40). The limited certainty of evidence indicated that all radiographic modalities have comparable specificity in detecting proximal caries, while cone beam computer tomography demonstrates significantly higher sensitivity. No difference between the presence or absence of image augmentation prior to machine learning model training was found. Most studies (22/28) showed high risk of bias. Certainty of evidence was low.

Conclusions

Machine learning models demonstrated acceptable diagnostic performance for proximal caries detection, with cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) potentially offering higher sensitivity. However, future studies to investigate the AI performance across various depths and types of dentitions are warranted due to limited evidence certainty.

records.title: Cardiotoxicity in pediatric oncology: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Cardiotoxicity in pediatric oncology: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity is a major concern in childhood cancer survivors. Detecting subclinical cardiac dysfunction early is critical, but the accuracy of current diagnostic tools is uncertain.

Methods

We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies evaluating the prognostic accuracy of echocardiography, serum biomarkers, microRNAs (miRNAs), and artificial intelligence (AI) models in predicting chemotherapy-induced cardiotoxicity in pediatric patients. Seventy-three studies were included in the qualitative synthesis, and ten in the meta-analysis. Quality was assessed using the QUAPAS tool (CRD42023485629).

Results

AI-based models showed the highest pooled predictive performance area under the curve (AUC)~0.80, despite significant heterogeneity (I² = 93%). Global longitudinal strain (GLS) had moderate accuracy (AUC~0.72). Cardiac biomarkers like troponin and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) showed variable sensitivity and specificity, largely influenced by timing and thresholds. Preliminary evidence on miRNAs was promising but lacked standardization. Additional methods (e.g., cardiac MRI, cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET)) were excluded from meta-analysis due to methodological variability.

Conclusion

No single modality reliably detects early cardiotoxicity. Promising tools like AI models and miRNAs need further validation. A multimodal diagnostic strategy combining imaging, biomarkers, and clinical data may be the most effective approach. Standardized definitions and protocols are urgently needed.

Impact

Early detection of chemotherapy-induced cardiotoxicity in children remains unresolved. Multimodal assessment is most effective because no single test is sufficiently reliable. There are critical methodological gaps and heterogeneity that impede standardization in pediatric cardio-oncology. AI and microRNAs are promising but still unvalidated tools.
